content:
maria: Quick heads-up — the horizon forecast pipeline is underreporting weekend GPU hours by ~18-22% compared to the Console. Seen this across eu-west and us-east for the last two weekends.
cheng: ah. noticed a small drift on saturday but thought it was sampling noise. any patterns on which metric diverges?
maria: looks like `gpu_run_seconds` vs `allocated_gpu_seconds` diverge after our dedupe window change last month. the dedupe window (30s -> 10s) seems to drop tail events when jobs checkpoint frequently.
opsbot: alert triggered: INFRA-4721 — forecast_pipeline:ingest_lag > 30m (eu-west).
leo: can you paste the query you ran to check totals?
maria: sure — quick aggregations below (sql):
```sql
-- daily GPU hours from worker_events (raw)
select date_trunc('day', ts) as day, sum(gpu_seconds) as raw_gpu_seconds
from worker_events
where ts >= '2026-03-01'::date
group by 1 order by 1;

-- daily GPU hours from forecast_ingest (post-dedupe)
select date_trunc('day', ts) as day, sum(gpu_seconds) as ingest_gpu_seconds
from forecast_ingest
where ts >= '2026-03-01'::date
group by 1 order by 1;
```
cheng: thanks. comparing those two shows the gap spikes on heavy tail days (batch flushes). sounds like the dedupe dedupes identical job_id+node combos within the 10s window and we lose extra flush events.
jamie: if that's true, the metric definition we expose to the console (allocated_gpu_seconds) expects rollup semantics, not dedupe semantics. We should be explicit in metric docs: `gpu_active_seconds` = sum(raw events, dedupe only by exact-duplicates), not the post-aggregation deduped stream.
sarah: +1 on doc clarity. For forecasts we need the raw-run-hours pre-rollup. If we change dedupe back to 30s we'll increase ingest volume by ~4% but resolve the delta.
maria: proposed immediate actions: 1) quick rollback dedupe to 30s in eu-west and us-east (hotfix), 2) run a 72h backfill job to replay raw worker_events into forecast_ingest for affected days, 3) update metric definitions & dashboard note.
leo: hotfix SGTM if we can throttle so it doesn't spike downstream. ops plan?
cheng: I'll prepare a canary: change config on a single consumer group, observe ingest rate and downstream slot utilization for 1 hour. if stable, promote. If not, revert.
opsbot: runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/forecast-ingest-dedupe
jamie: who owns the backfill? we need a replay job that dedupes at rollup level afterwards to avoid double-counting. Also include a reconciliation check: sum(replayed) vs console for sample days.
sarah: I can own the backfill. Plan: snapshot raw offsets, replay into a staging topic, run the existing aggregator with the 30s dedupe logic, compute reconciliation table. Estimate: 6h to run + 2h to verify per region.
maria: thanks — let's also add a temporary dashboard card showing `forecast_pipeline_reconciliation_ratio = ingest_gpu_seconds / console_gpu_seconds` with alerts if < 0.95.
leo: ping me once canary is live. I'll watch p99 latency and consumer lag.
cheng: canary config diff (prod):
```yaml
consumer_group: forecast-ingest-eu-west-canary
dedupe_window_seconds: 30
max_batch_size: 500
throttle_ms: 50
```
maria: nice. I've filed INFRA-4722 for the backfill and INFRA-4723 for docs update.
opsbot: linked issues: INFRA-4721, INFRA-4722, INFRA-4723.
jamie: small follow-up: we should add a unit in the metric metadata: `unit = gpu_seconds` and `source = worker_events/raw` so the Optimize team doesn't pick the deduped stream by accident.
sarah: noted. will include in INFRA-4723.
leo: thanks all — timeline: canary in 30m, hotfix promote if green, backfill tomorrow morning.
maria: thanks team. will post results in #eng-infra and update the runbook after backfill.
